title: Decoding with Limits::none() allocates the length a prefix claims before reading the body (up to 4 GiB per prefix)

target.versions_affected: 28.0.0 - 30.0.0 when decoding with Limits::none() (28.0.0, 28.0.1 and 30.0.0 executed; lower bound not established)

severity_basis: Hardening: in stellar-xdr 30.0.0 and main ebec5fb, BytesM, StringM and VecM<u8> allocate vec![0u8; len] before read_exact (#581 fixed only the generic VecM<T>). No SDF service is known to decode untrusted input with Limits::none(): rs-soroban-env uses DEFAULT_XDR_RW_LIMITS (depth 500, len 32 MiB); stellar-rpc's xdr2json and preflight use the same 32 MiB; rs-stellar-archivist sets len to the input length; only offline CLIs use none(). Without a memory cap the allocation is lazy (clean UnexpectedEof); under RLIMIT_AS 1 GiB the process aborts.
caps_note: No CAP applies: an XDR encoding rule that holds in every protocol version (the corpus's xdr-strict group).

entries.expected: reject without allocating more than the input can hold
entries.observed: Executed on 28.0.0, 28.0.1 and 30.0.0 under limits-none (Limits::none()) with RLIMIT_AS 1 GiB: the process aborts allocating the length the prefix claims ('memory allocation of … bytes failed'). Under limits-default the length budget refuses the input before allocating; without a memory cap the allocation is lazy and the decode is refused (UnexpectedEof).

evidence.pre_fix: Conformance runner (xcc conform run --columns 'rust@*' --entries 'xdr-strict/length-prefix-exceeds-input.*'), L0: every Rust column runs these entries in a fresh driver process under RLIMIT_AS 1 GiB (the known divergence's profile, limits-none under address-space cap RLIMIT_AS 1 GiB); the limits-none columns crash, the limits-default columns refuse (LengthLimitExceeded).
evidence.expected_basis: A decoder must not allocate more than the remaining input can hold: stellar-core's xdrpp checks the length against the remaining bytes before resizing (marshal.h), and go-xdr fixed the same shape in stellar/go-xdr#34.

reproduction.method: Re-assessed in a separate run on stellar-xdr 30.0.0 and main ebec5fb: BytesM, StringM and VecM<u8> allocate the claimed length before reading under Limits::none(); without a memory cap the allocation is lazy, under RLIMIT_AS 1 GiB the process aborts; Limits::len(8) refuses before allocating.

queries: repo:stellar/rs-stellar-xdr allocation (PR #581 limits VecM capacity only; BytesM still allocates up front)

approval.scope: Public hardening issue on stellar/rs-stellar-xdr (#623): BytesM, StringM and VecM<u8> pre-allocate the length prefix under Limits::none().

history.note: Created from a run of the probe's memory vectors through the Rust conformance driver under an address-space cap; no public issue or advisory found.
Assessed as low (hardening): no SDF service is known to decode untrusted input with Limits::none().
